subject: Execution sites, subprocessors, and cross-border evidence — Helio Health Q&A
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@heliohealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Helio Health Legal <legal@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T14:03:00Z
Subject: Quick Q — where does Helio data get executed / cross-border transfers?

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Legal and our infra team have a couple of focused questions before we can move to procurement: where exactly do LLM requests for Helio accounts execute (region/hypervisor level), which subprocessors might touch the request, and are there any scenarios that would cause data to leave the US?

Specifically:
- Runtime regions and primary subprocessors per region
- Any routing fallback rules that could move traffic to another region (and why)
- KMS ownership and whether keys are customer-managed in Private/Dedicated deployments
- Typical retention/TTL for request data and the process for verified deletion (audit evidence)

Would appreciate a short evidence pack we can attach to our vendor assessment. If you have a short summary PDF and a checklist of the documents/legal artifacts you can provide that would help.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security & Privacy
Helio Health

--
Helio Health (external)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T18:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where does Helio data get executed / cross-border transfers?

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answer up front: for Helio's account we can pin your workload to US-only execution (primary us-east-1) and apply customer-managed KMS keys for Private/Dedicated deployments. We will not intentionally export request payloads outside the pinned region unless you opt into cross-region failover for resilience.

I've attached a 1‑page residency summary (residency-summary.pdf) and flagged this to Marissa + Hannah to assemble the evidence packet (SOC/SLA excerpts, subprocessor roster, network routing diagram, and deletion audit sample).

Action items:
- Marissa: can you prepare the evidence bundle and include a sample deletion audit showing the erase timeline?
- Hannah: please confirm the subprocessor roster and the exact regions for our hosted fallback zones.

Elena, I can get you an initial package by end of day tomorrow. If we need a formal DPA / DocuSign flow we can route that to your legal contact.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: residency-summary.pdf (1 page)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where does Helio data get executed / cross-border transfers?

Elena / Vivek — attaching the enumerated evidence below and in the attached archive (evidence-packet-helio.zip). Long answer (concise bullet points):

1) Runtime execution locations
- Hosted: primary execution in AWS us-east-1 (control plane in us-east-1); optional execution in us-west-2 for regional redundancy only by request.
- Dedicated: customer-dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1 (you can reserve capacity there).
- Private (VPC): deployed into customer VPC in their preferred region; we provide an installer image and KMS integration.

2) Subprocessors and roles
- AWS (Amazon Web Services) — primary compute and object storage in us-east-1 (redwood-inference account), networking transit via AWS backbone.
- FastPipelines (contracted edge caching) — transient caches for prompt prefix caching, cache TTLs < 1 hour for non-persistent workloads.
- LogStore Inc (managed telemetry store) — stores anonymized traces and operational metrics (PII redaction by default).
- Optional GCP europe-west-1 and Azure apac-east instances only if customer enables cross-region failover.

3) Cross-border / export controls
- Default behavior for Helio: we will pin execution to US-only. Cross-region execution is opt-in and requires explicit agreement (route-level config + written approval).
- Fallback policy: if you enable multi-region resilience, requests may be routed to your configured secondary region; otherwise no automatic cross-border routing.

4) KMS and keys
- Hosted: keys are managed by Redwood KMS (HSM-backed), customers can opt for Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) in Dedicated/Private through an integration (we provide key-wrapping instructions).
- Private: full BYOK (bring-your-own-key) support; logs show KMS operations for audit. Included: kms-key-ownership.md

5) Retention and deletion
- Request logs and transient models: default retention 30 days for hosted telemetry; request payloads (non-PII by default) persisted for 7 days for analytics unless otherwise configured.
- Customer-controlled retention: Dedicated/Private deployments can set TTLs down to 24 hours for request payloads.
- Deletion process: verified deletion includes background wipe + manifest entry in our audit trail; we can provide a signed deletion certificate for erasure events. We generally commit to erasure within 72 hours of a verified request for Dedicated/Private, and 7 days for Hosted unless otherwise contractually agreed.

6) Evidence we included in | evidence-packet-helio.zip |
- Subprocessor roster (signed contracts redacted)
- Network routing diagram (region and transit hops)
- Sample deletion certificate and audit log extract
- SOC excerpt and data processing addendum template

If you want hardened contractual language (SLA for 72-hour erasure) we can add that into the DPA.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-packet-helio.zip, kms-key-ownership.md
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@heliohealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Helio Health Legal <legal@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where does Helio data get executed / cross-border transfers?

Vivek / Marissa — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups from legal and infra after reviewing the packet: 

- Legal wants a DPA with a specific 72-hour deletion SLA for Dedicated deployments and an obligation to provide a signed deletion certificate within 5 business days of erasure. Please send a DocuSign link to our legal contact (legal@heliohealth.com).
- Infra asks for the sample deletion audit (anonymized) that shows the manifest records that prove erasure. The extract you referenced should be sufficient if it includes timestamps and KMS operation IDs.
- Can you confirm that enabling CMK in Dedicated gives us the ability to revoke access immediately (i.e., destroy key material) and that Redwood will provide a key-wrapping audit?

If you can route the DPA and the audit extract today we'd like to start procurement next week.

Thanks again,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security & Privacy
Helio Health
